args.text: Sending of emails (registration, forgot password, invitations, single and bulk recognition emails) currently happens synchronously inside the web request through Amazon SES, so slow or failing delivery blocks and breaks user-facing calls. Move it to background processing with Celery on an SQS queue. Code that sends emails must keep calling the same email interface and return immediately after the job is queued; the actual delivery happens in a separate worker process, which keeps the existing behaviour of using a mock client in local and test environments and the real SES client elsewhere. Task payloads must be JSON-serializable and validated, each kind of email gets its own task, and failed deliveries must still be logged and are retried according to the queue's visibility timeout. In the test environment tasks must execute immediately in the same process so existing tests keep working without a broker. The broker address and the queue location come from the application settings, with defaults that work against the local development stack (LocalStack). Also set up a scheduled job that fires every day at 14:00 UTC and for now only logs that the daily report was triggered. Add the dependency, and make the local environment and container setup able to run the worker and the scheduler. After the plan is accepted, run ambicode:task with the arguments: --task rl-k12-cec --headless "Go ahead with the plan. Do not run builds, tests, linters or reviews."
